notes: Novel capability — Live Preview for Contentstack CMS content across GO, UP, MX brands. The useContent hook (hooks/useContent) is the central content provider consumed by 38+ components and is the natural attachment point for streaming real-time preview updates. The Brand enum in src/constants/common.ts defines the three-brand scope. Contentstack API hosts are unreachable at test time, so VCs stop at our side of that boundary.

after.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS

notes: Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria with useful context about the useContent hook attachment point, Brand enum scope, and Contentstack API boundary. Since there were no ACs to review, I created the full set from scratch. Key design decisions: (1) ACs 5-7 cover each brand explicitly rather than a single parameterized AC, because each brand must be independently verifiable. (2) ACs 3-4 address connection lifecycle — disconnection must not blank the page, and reconnection must be automatic. (3) ACs 9 and 16 address security — XSS injection and information leakage from error responses. (4) AC 12 addresses the debouncing/throttling concern without specifying implementation. (5) AC 13 ensures the feature is toggleable. (6) AC 14 prevents resource leaks. (7) AC 17-18 cover edge cases around missing references and unknown content types. CAVEAT: File contents were unavailable — my criteria are based solely on the story title, description, and file paths. If useContent, common.ts, contentstack.ts, or the mock/interface files contain constraints that affect these ACs, they may need adjustment.

notes: Openspec provided empty ACs, so all criteria are new. Derived from the story title '[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS' which implies real-time draft content rendering in a CMS preview context. Criteria cover: basic rendering (AC1), real-time update latency (AC2), rapid-edit debouncing/coalescing (AC3), empty/null field handling (AC4), large payload resilience (AC5), service error handling (AC6), timeout handling (AC7), authorization/security (AC8), navigation state persistence (AC9), multi-locale support per the GO/UP/MX market scope (AC10), save/publish continuity (AC11), and broken asset resilience (AC12). Without access to technical notes, codebase, or existing preview implementation, these are best-effort criteria; some may need adjustment once the actual CMS integration (e.g., Contentstack) and preview architecture are known.
